prompt: A delivery company's on-time rate fell from 96% to 88% in six months. Order volume rose 25% over the same period. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: On-time delivery fell from 96% to 88% while volume rose 25%.
options.feedback: This restates the facts without proposing a cause.

options.text: It could be traffic, drivers, the routing software, weather, the warehouse or the volume increase.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: The company needs more drivers; the volume increase is definitely the cause.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.

options.text: Capacity likely hasn't kept up with volume, so routes are overloaded.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd compare on-time rates by route against stops per driver.

explanation: Volume rose 25% while on-time performance fell, which points to capacity. Testing on-time rates against driver load confirms or rejects it.

distractor_flaws.M.restates_facts: On-time delivery fell from 96% to 88% while volume rose 25%.
distractor_flaws.M.shotgun_hypotheses: It could be traffic, drivers, the routing software, weather, the warehouse or the volume increase.
distractor_flaws.M.overconfident_hypothesis: The company needs more drivers; the volume increase is definitely the cause.
